title: Ensured Project Handbook
body:
Reviewed November 1, 2026. Status: current implementation and planned work are distinguished below. Documentation is not certification of production readiness.

Ensured is an insurance and reinsurance platform whose first goal is to help insurers, MGAs, brokers and cedents turn fragmented submissions into reviewable underwriting decisions. Its longer-term goal is to connect approved risks with eligible capital and support the resulting contracts, servicing and financial obligations.

How to use this handbook

SectionQuestions answered
01 Product Vision and GoalsWhy build Ensured? Who uses it? What defines a successful pilot?
02 Platform ArchitectureWhich services own each responsibility? How do documents, identity and decisions flow?
03 Data and Financial ModelsWhat do the records and calculations mean? How are party obligations, cash and risk distinguished?
04 Delivery and QualityWhat exists, what remains, and where is the Jira work?
05 Operations and MaintenanceHow is the workspace developed, configured, released and recovered?

Project state at this review

The repository contains working foundations for accounts/gateway, KYC review, document processing, generated submission forms, human feedback, modeling/pricing, commercial records, quotes/signatures/binding and network collaboration. This does not establish a complete end-to-end production product. Party financial reconciliation, funding/settlement, model input correctness, release reproducibility and several marketplace actions remain tracked work.

Evidence and terminology

  • Implemented means a relevant source path or documented service exists; it does not imply deployed, fully tested or legally approved.
  • Verified means a specific check was actually run and its scope is named. Planned means acceptance criteria are tracked in Jira.
  • Capacity is permission/availability to assume risk. A commitment is a promise. Funding is received capital. Allocation/deployment is use of capital. Settlement is a confirmed financial transfer.
  • Seed fixtures, illustrative metrics, snapshots, contract approvals and provider acceptance must not be described as proof of paid cash or production readiness.

Documentation structure

true3

Delivery ownership

Jira AIN is the delivery system. AIN-1 through AIN-12 track completion areas; AIN-47 coordinates data-model improvements. Individual owners, estimates, launch thresholds and dates require delivery planning and are not invented here.

title: 01 Product Vision and Goals
body:
Reviewed November 1, 2026. Status: current implementation and planned work are distinguished below. Documentation is not certification of production readiness.

Mission

Make an underwriting team productive before the marketplace has significant capital liquidity. The primary value is turning messy inbound risk information into consistent, reviewable submissions with explicit evidence, appetite decisions, loss estimates and pricing. Capital matching is an expansion of this foundation, not a prerequisite for useful insurer software.

Strategic goals

  1. Unify document/email/portal intake and reduce repeated manual transcription without discarding source evidence.
  2. Support any configured risk class through taxonomy, organization-editable schema and selected modeling/rating methods.
  3. Make every financial or risk number explainable through method, inputs, assumptions and revision history.
  4. Provide human review and explicit approvals for underwriting, signatures, binding and financial actions.
  5. Connect eligible counterparties to governed facilities, commitments and ultimately reconciled settlement and servicing.

Business model direction

The near-term roadmap identifies organization/seat subscriptions and usage-based services as the insurer-side revenue opportunity. Marketplace placement fees, asset-management fees, trading and data products are later possibilities, not all implemented revenue streams. Technical premium is the cost of transferred risk; it must not be confused with platform revenue.

Architectural principles

  • Risk class is configuration/data, not a special-case engine branch for each line of business.
  • Extend working models and use additive, backward-compatible migrations.
  • Pin immutable reviewed versions so a schema or data correction cannot silently change past decisions.
  • Use AI assistance with clear provenance and explicit fallback behavior; do not imply unsupported confidence or automatic approval.
  • Keep tenant authorization, identity ownership and evidence handling at explicit service boundaries.

title: 01.1 Participants and End-to-End Journeys
body:
Reviewed November 1, 2026. Status: current implementation and planned work are distinguished below. Documentation is not certification of production readiness.

ParticipantPrimary needRelevant boundary
Insured / submitting partyProvide risk facts, review terms, accept or sign an identified versionA saved party/contact is not automatically a verified legal identity or payout mandate.
Broker / MGAPrepare submissions, coordinate terms and parties, track remunerationIntermediary identity, commission entitlement and payment recipient must be explicit.
Insurer / underwriter / cedentAssess appetite, price risk, approve/bind, manage retained/ceded exposureModel output supports a decision; it does not itself approve or bind.
Reinsurer / retrocessionaire / capacity providerSet terms, approve participation and control aggregate exposureAvailable capacity, reserved capacity and funded capital are separate.
Investor / SPV / custodianUnderstand commitments, capital calls, holdings, collateral and returnsCurrent models exist; reconciled funding and distributions remain completion work.
Reviewer / operator / platform administratorReview evidence, resolve exceptions and operate the platformAdministrative ability is distinct from financial approval authority.

Insurer pilot journey

  1. Authenticate, establish permitted organization context and complete required onboarding/evidence checks.
  2. Configure a risk class, schema, appetite and model/rating parameters.
  3. Receive documents; process them into structured evidence and generated sections.
  4. Review/correct the workbench; preserve the selected source revision and feedback history.
  5. Run underwriting/modeling, inspect uncertainty, resolve capacity and capture an approved quote snapshot.
  6. Deliver terms, record acceptance/signatures and use the existing binding workflow where permitted.
  7. Hand the bound financial and contractual evidence to servicing and billing; close the remaining handoff gaps through Jira.

Capital release journey

Publish an eligible opportunity → inspect immutable documents and risk assumptions → propose/approve participation → create a commitment → call and confirm funds → allocate/collateralize → service premiums and claims → approve and reconcile distributions. Several transitions currently have only partial implementation or data models; AIN-8 through AIN-10 own completion.

Exception journeys

  • Unreadable/conflicting documents remain reviewable rather than silently becoming zero/known facts.
  • Expired eligibility, changed terms, unavailable capacity and failed providers must block or refer the relevant action.
  • Corrections and reversals append history; actors should never “fix” settled money by deleting records.

Delivery: AIN-6 · AIN-7 · AIN-8 · AIN-10

title: 01.2 Scope, Milestones and Success Criteria
body:
Reviewed November 1, 2026. Status: current implementation and planned work are distinguished below. Documentation is not certification of production readiness.

Release scope

MilestoneOutcomeEvidence required
Insurer pilotNon-seeded intake through reviewed underwriting, pricing, capacity, quote/bind and servicing handoffTwo unlike configured risk classes; reproducible inputs; explicit approvals and observable failure recovery.
Capital marketplace releaseFunctional discovery/allocation plus reconciled funding, collateral and payout servicingEligible parties, idempotent provider integration, balanced statements and tested reversals.
Later product expansionAdditional lines, vendors, analytics and secondary-market capabilitiesSeparate product decisions and validation; model/table existence is insufficient.

What completion means

  • A fresh checkout builds compatible services and packages with the required checks passing.
  • Each demonstrated outcome uses actual persisted workflow evidence rather than seed/demo shortcuts.
  • Financial figures distinguish estimate, commitment, receivable/payable, receipt, deployment and settlement.
  • Reviewers can reproduce a decision from its immutable inputs, schema, model and approval history.
  • Tenant separation, concurrency, provider failure, restore and rollback are tested with documented results.

Measurement plan

Measure intake success by format, extraction correction rate, time from intake to reviewed quote, failed/retried jobs, model input coverage, quote-to-bind completion, reconciliation exceptions, latency and processing cost. Establish baselines and agree thresholds before claiming a target is met; no numerical launch SLA has been approved by this review.

Scope boundaries

EnsuredLogistics is a separate freight collaboration product in the workspace. It is not the insurance transaction lifecycle and should have its own product/release documentation. Licenses, regulatory acceptance, external vendor contracts and custody arrangements require accountable business decisions. This handbook does not assert they have been obtained.

title: 02 Platform Architecture
body:
Reviewed November 1, 2026. Status: current implementation and planned work are distinguished below. Documentation is not certification of production readiness.

System shape

The parent workspace coordinates independent repositories/submodules. EnsuredUI hosts the user-facing application and built microfrontends. EnsuredAuth/gateway establishes identity; EnsuredAPI owns marketplace/business workflows and orchestrates supporting services. Pipeline packages provide stage implementations and shared persistence contracts. Dedicated services retain their own identity, KYC, feedback, network or connector responsibilities.

Primary request and data flow

  1. Browser requests reach the configured public gateway and UI origin.
  2. Accounts verify the session; the gateway forwards short-lived request-bound assertions to the intended service.
  3. The owning service checks role, organization, record access and operation policy.
  4. Document operations persist job/execution/artifact history; human edits create separate feedback versions.
  5. Approved workflows freeze snapshots and produce commercial/financial records; external integrations require explicit completion and reconciliation semantics.

Persistence boundaries

Shared local PostgreSQL infrastructure does not imply a shared ownership model. Identity and KYC have separate logical databases; Network owns its records; Feedback owns its schema and version history. API/pipeline data and commercial SQL migrations coexist in the marketplace boundary. Services should communicate through contracts rather than reading each other’s private tables.

Composition and deployment

Marketplace and Network frontends are consumed as built packages in the host. Updating a microfrontend requires rebuilding the host; this is not runtime module federation. Auth supports combined Worker and Node configurations as well as older separate processes. Deployment configuration must identify which supported topology is actually used.

Architecture changes in progress

AIN-47 formalizes ownership, relationship integrity and schema contracts. AIN-52 defines reliable cross-service event handoffs; AIN-53 defines rebuildable read projections. These planned additions must preserve existing API and audit behavior.

title: 02.2 Submission Pipeline and Human Review
body:
Reviewed November 1, 2026. Status: current implementation and planned work are distinguished below. Documentation is not certification of production readiness.

Processing stages

Stage groupPurposePersistence / caveat
Ingestion and ingestionAmqpAccept documents/messages and envelope/channel metadataPreserve source identity and tenant attribution.
OCR, classification, extractionRead source content and derive typed evidenceQuality depends on format/provider; retain confidence and source versions.
Subject, location and financial discoveryIdentify entities/exposures, geography and financial factsDiscovery is evidence, not automatic validation of economic meaning.
Normalization and validationCanonical mapping, schema validation, appetite/scrub signalsConfigured taxonomy and honest unknown states are required.
Schema generationBuild reviewable sections using organization schemas and component contractsAI-generated sections must satisfy structural and component capability constraints.
Pre-rating, risk compute and capacityAssist underwriting, calculate models/pricing and evaluate capacityRating/underwriting remain manual in the documented job flow; stage capacity is not yet treaty-ledger integrated.
Workflow, oracle attestation and storage/searchWorkflow/output support and downstream artifactsDo not assume every stage is complete: StorageSearch is currently a passthrough.

Automatic and manual execution

The documented worker scans committed submissions every five seconds and waits fifteen seconds after the latest file before queuing document processing. A finalized ingestion/upload event and at least one file are required. Automatic work follows configured dependencies through schema generation. Organizations, or independent users for their own submissions, can disable automatic document processing; manual advance/rerun remains available.

Jobs and failure semantics

Advance/rerun requests return HTTP 202 with a job. PostgreSQL stores queued/running/completed/failed states; locks and a partial unique index coordinate one active job per submission. A running job interrupted after its execution lock disappears is marked failed, not blindly replayed, because stage work can be partially persisted. Review the failed execution and explicitly rerun where appropriate.

Human corrections and replay

Feedback stores full append-only snapshots, actor/time, expected version, parent and original execution. A restore appends a new version. New pipeline runs do not overwrite an existing human workbench. Organization picklist publication and feedback commits use separate service transactions; a partial failure may require reconciliation rather than rerunning the whole action.

Completion work

Align canonical, workbench and model revisions; retain field-level money/party provenance; implement searchable artifacts and scalable projections. Preserve {ok:false} stage failures and lineage rather than replacing them with successful empty results.

title: 02.3 Identity, Authorization and Evidence Boundaries
body:
Reviewed November 1, 2026. Status: current implementation and planned work are distinguished below. Documentation is not certification of production readiness.

Authentication versus authorization

Accounts owns credential/session identity. The marketplace owns business roles and organization membership. The gateway strips untrusted identity headers and forwards signed, short-lived, request-bound assertions with service-specific audiences. Each service must still authorize the requested record and action. Supplying organizationId is not proof of membership.

KYC and legal-party evidence

KYC is a manual evidence/review service. Applicants submit drafts and credentials; independent authorized reviewers record evidence checks and case decisions. Approval requires the documented evidence and a valid expiry. Expired approvals are reported expired; historical decisions remain intact. The service does not itself claim automated AML, sanctions, accreditation, liveness or license-registry checks.

Signatures and binding

Signing uses explicit reviewed snapshots, hashes and verified ceremonies. A guest invitation proves possession of the scoped invitation and signing credential, not independently checked legal identity. A signature alone is not binding. A separate binding workflow exists with role checks, signature/quote readiness, immutable snapshots and a transaction lock. Manual/no-quote paths and financial completeness need an explicit policy.

Network and connectors

Network discoverability is opt-in; company publishing requires membership and an explicit grant. Its private marketplace projection excludes credentials and KYC evidence. Email service requests use service authentication; mailbox tokens/checkpoints remain owned by the API and must not appear in logs or documentation.

Unfinished financial controls

  • Versioned eligibility checks before publication, commitment, binding and payout.
  • Beneficiary/payout-account mandates and independently authorized changes.
  • Clear separation between posting actor, legal contracting party, payer, payee and beneficial owner.
  • Expiry/revocation/provider-outage behavior and auditable exception approvals.

title: 03 Data and Financial Models
body:
Reviewed November 1, 2026. Status: current implementation and planned work are distinguished below. Documentation is not certification of production readiness.

Purpose

This section connects technical records to business meaning. The current code contains substantial models and immutable evidence, but separate balance fields and event lists do not automatically reconcile into a party-level ledger. Use the child pages to distinguish source facts, decisions, contractual obligations and cash movements.

Four layers of data

LayerExamplesRequired interpretation
Observed factsDocuments, extracted premium/TIV/loss, party/address, currencySource, unit, confidence, period and conflict status.
Decisions and versionsCanonical/workbench revision, model run, pricing version, approvalExact inputs, method/schema version, actor and assumptions.
Contractual obligationsQuote, binding, facility, commitment, premium due, claim/recoveryLegal party roles, effective terms, payer/payee and obligation state.
Financial executionReceipt, funding, collateral transfer, payment, reversalProvider evidence, currency, settlement status and reconciliation.

Data principles

  • Unknown is not zero; committed is not funded; approved is not paid.
  • Use explicit currency and precision. Do not aggregate currencies without a cited FX policy and rate timestamp.
  • Preserve immutable history; corrections/reversals are new referenced records.
  • Separate ownership and authorization from display labels and free-text party names.
  • Use typed relational constraints for core identity/money/references while retaining validated versioned organization extensions.
  • Each field needs an authoritative writer and a documented dependency/rebuild policy.

Delivery

AIN-47 coordinates shared schema design and integrity; domain tickets remain in their original epics. AIN-34, AIN-35 and AIN-18 establish the party, money and lineage contracts on which the rest depends.

Delivery: AIN-47 · AIN-34 · AIN-35 · AIN-18

title: 03.2 Party Financial Flows and Accounting Semantics
body:
Reviewed November 1, 2026. Status: current implementation and planned work are distinguished below. Documentation is not certification of production readiness.

Party responsibilities

Party / roleFinancial quantities to distinguish
Insured / policyholderQuoted premium, premium payable, receipt applied, taxes/fees and refunds.
Broker / MGACollected premium, commission entitlement, remittance payable and outstanding balances.
Insurer / cedentGross premium/loss, retained risk, ceded premium, reinsurance payable and recoverables.
Reinsurer / retrocessionaireAssumed/retroceded exposure, premium entitlement, reserves and claims/recoveries.
Investor / SPV / custodianCommitted, called, received, allocated/deployed, collateralized, distributable and paid capital.
PlatformSubscription/usage receivables and platform fees; distinguish pass-through premium from revenue.

Existing capacity accounting

Commercial capacity entries record reserve, allocate, release, refer and close_referral. Exact cent arithmetic calculates outstanding reservations and allocations. Allocation against a reservation moves usage rather than adding a second exposure; releases reference an earlier entry. Aggregate, risk and occurrence limits constrain usage. This is risk-capacity accounting, not bank settlement.

Existing servicing accounting

Servicing stores report obligations, premium due/paid, claims, claim reductions, recoveries and renewals. Summaries group by currency and contract: premium outstanding = due − paid; recognized claims = claims − reductions; recoverable = recognized claims − recoveries. These calculations do not determine treaty entitlement from a gross loss and do not identify both payer/payee accounts.

Target premium and capital flows

  1. Capture gross premium, commission/tax/fee basis and currency from approved terms.
  2. Create linked party receivables/payables with exact contract/revision and due date.
  3. Record provider-confirmed receipts separately from promises and allocate them to obligations.
  4. Distribute net amounts under the approved rules, preserving rounding residuals and evidence.
  5. Reconcile statements and append reversals/corrections when needed; never rewrite historical payments.

Illustrative conservation example — not a product tariff

If an approved USD 1,000 premium has a USD 100 intermediary commission and USD 20 platform fee, the remaining USD 880 is attributable to the contractual recipient before any separately defined tax or other split. All three sides must total USD 1,000. This example explains conservation only; actual terms, payer direction, tax treatment and recognition policy must be configured and approved.

Confirmed display issues and missing capabilities

Investor dashboards currently count pending commitments as funded/invested and include unowned opportunities in a weighted return labeled IRR. Capital models lack consistent currency fields. Target party ledgers, commission semantics, settlement reconciliation and immutable payment reversals are tracked separately.

title: 03.3 Risk, Pricing and Return Calculation Models
body:
Reviewed November 1, 2026. Status: current implementation and planned work are distinguished below. Documentation is not certification of production readiness.

MethodInputs / calculationLimits and interpretation
Generic loss costExpected loss = exposure base × configured/benchmark loss rateBasis and unit must match; the method name generic_burning_cost does not prove experience has been collected.
Generic ratingTechnical premium = expected loss / target loss ratioRequires positive target ratio and valid loss input; not a universal tariff.
Credibility blendZ=min(1,sqrt(n/nFull)); blend experience and priorCurrent compute supplies null experience and n=0; it remains prior driven.
Cat exposureDeclared event set and damage inputs → event losses → seeded Monte Carlo EP/tail metricsSimplified/cited inputs are not a licensed-vendor-quality certification; preserve source and seed.
ParametricDeclared exceedance/trigger probability and payout functionBasis risk and source quality remain explicit; modeled payout is not an executed claim payment.
Casualty ILFConfigured increased-limit factors modify supported rating inputsThis is not proof of a complete loss-development/IBNR reserving product.
Risk/return fieldsriskScore uses loss/premium; expectedReturn uses marginTargetUnderwriting margin is not investor IRR or guaranteed return.

Required provenance

A reproducible financial result needs the selected risk class/method, canonical/effective revision, exposure basis and currency, prior source/citation, model parameters, model version, simulated seed when relevant, confidence/flags and reviewer decision. A bare decimal or chart is insufficient.

Confirmed correctness defects

  • deriveExposure currently selects TIV before revenue/payroll even when another basis is declared; the isolated revenue fixture produced a tenfold exposure error.
  • Unavailable technicalPremium becomes numeric zero in persistence; some consumers mask flags but the value remains ambiguous. Legitimate approved zero-price terms must remain distinguishable.
  • ModelRun/PricingVersion/current pointer/metrics are written without one encompassing transaction, creating a partial-write/concurrency risk; database fault-injection remains to be done.

Validation and governance

Maintain known-answer fixtures, parameter bounds, currency/basis checks and independent actuarial review for launch methods. Import only qualified experience with valuation periods and gross/net meaning. Model approval, quote approval, contractual binding and payment execution are different decisions and should retain separate evidence.

title: 03.4 Data Model Improvement Plan
body:
Reviewed November 1, 2026. Status: current implementation and planned work are distinguished below. Documentation is not certification of production readiness.

Foundation epic

AIN-47 owns shared model architecture and database integrity. It complements the existing financial domain work rather than moving or duplicating those tickets. Implementation should preserve organization-editable schemas and existing immutable audit records.

TicketDeliverable
AIN-48As-is/to-be ERDs, field dictionary, cardinalities, tenant scope and authoritative service/writer.
AIN-49Tenant-safe references, uniqueness, valid-state constraints and concurrency invariants.
AIN-50Typed core versus JSONB extension boundaries, schema versions and old/new compatibility.
AIN-51Immutable dependency references and occurrence/recording/effective/valuation time semantics.
AIN-52Versioned cross-service event envelopes, outbox/inbox, idempotency and replay contracts.
AIN-53Indexed/rebuildable party-balance and submission projections with checkpoints.
AIN-54Additive expand/backfill/validate/cutover migrations and reconciliation reports.
AIN-55Schema drift, direct-write integrity and migration contract checks in CI.

Recommended implementation order

  1. Agree party/account, currency and revision semantics with AIN-34, AIN-35 and AIN-18; produce the ownership map first.
  2. Add typed references/constraints and validated extension schemas without breaking existing readers.
  3. Implement version/event handoff contracts with domain workflow owners.
  4. Backfill representative legacy records using reviewed mappings; retain unresolved values instead of fabricated defaults.
  5. Build/rebuild projections and measure query plans at agreed loads.
  6. Validate migration, application compatibility, financial reconciliation and rollback before production cutover.

Acceptance boundaries

A schema task is not complete merely because a migration applies. It must demonstrate valid historical records remain readable; invalid direct writes are rejected; same-tenant references hold; duplicated operations cannot double-post; projected balances can be rebuilt; and financial totals reconcile by party/currency. Separate-service references need explicit contract validation rather than impossible cross-database foreign keys.

title: 04 Delivery and Quality
body:
Reviewed November 1, 2026. Status: current implementation and planned work are distinguished below. Documentation is not certification of production readiness.

Delivery structure

AIN is the project of record. Thirteen epics organize completion and data-model improvements. The finance audit added 34 child tickets: 11 Bugs and 23 Tasks labeled gap. AIN-47 adds eight data-model implementation Tasks. Existing issue parents were retained and cross-cutting schema work is linked through relationships.

Prioritization

P0/P1 values in descriptions and labels are planning priorities, not estimates or promised release dates. Fix pricing-input correctness and payment/plan authorization issues alongside the party/currency/revision foundation. Work on complete evidence-backed journeys rather than treating the existence of a page or model as completion.

Required evidence for Done

  • A concrete user-visible outcome and approved data/financial semantics.
  • Meaningful tests at the responsible service boundary, including negative authorization and failure cases.
  • Migration and compatibility proof for persisted-model changes.
  • Source/build versions and linked reviewer evidence.
  • Known limitations, operational recovery behavior and documentation updates.

Documentation maintenance

Update the owning Confluence child page when behavior changes, link the delivery ticket and name the verification performed. Keep observed findings separate from proposed design. Mark stale historical documents explicitly; never use a past “complete” summary to infer current production readiness.

title: 05 Operations and Maintenance
body:
Reviewed November 1, 2026. Status: current implementation and planned work are distinguished below. Documentation is not certification of production readiness.

Workspace development

  1. Clone the parent with recursive submodules, or initialize existing submodules before building.
  2. Inspect current package manifests and lockfiles; install dependencies per package with the required private-registry access.
  3. Use Node 24 for the reviewed workspace; check individual package engine constraints when changing runtime.
  4. Configure service-local environment files using each .env.example, with secrets held outside version control.
  5. Start the shared local database and required owning-service migrations, then run the selected application topology.
  6. Build shared UI dependencies and the host together; verify health and one authorized user journey.

Root commands and scope

CommandPurpose / prerequisite
npm run docker:databaseDiscover local service database declarations and start/provision the shared development PostgreSQL server; does not replace application migrations.
npm run docker:servicesStart documented application containers; helper expects supporting local containers/configuration described in README.
npm run setup:ui / npm run build:uiInstall/build UI dependencies and host; private package access may be required.
npm run start:api / npm run start:gatewayRun the separate local Node development topology.
npm run pipeline:setup / pipeline:build / pipeline:testPrepare and validate pipeline packages; inspect script behavior before using against live services.
npm run pipeline:verifyParity/component-policy gate; currently has a tracked failure.
npm run test:auth / test:kyc / test:email / network:testTargeted owning-service checks; use isolated databases as required.

Working-tree and release discipline

The reviewed workspace contains modified submodules and uncommitted local work. Capture reviewed source commits and compatible package versions before release. Do not assume local builds represent pinned parent revisions. Commit changes in the owning child repository and then update the parent pin.

Operational ownership

Each service owns its health, configuration, migrations, secrets and recovery procedure. The service catalog helps observe/discover endpoints; it cannot certify a financial transaction. Define on-call ownership and escalation routes during delivery planning rather than embedding unassigned people into this documentation.

title: 05.1 Configuration, Release and Recovery Runbook
body:
Reviewed November 1, 2026. Status: current implementation and planned work are distinguished below. Documentation is not certification of production readiness.

Configuration boundaries

AreaOperational contract
Identity/gatewayConfigure public origin and request-signing secrets for the selected topology. Combined Worker and separate Node deployments have different requirements; follow the Auth guide.
DatabaseService-local database URL/credentials; shared local server does not grant permission to read another service’s private schema.
EmailConnector secret and registry discovery; outbound provider/sender settings. Provider acceptance is not inbox delivery.
KYC / Network / FeedbackDistinct service secrets, scopes and URLs. Do not expose trusted internal data endpoints directly to browsers.
Private packagesProvide registry token through the supported environment mechanism, never a committed literal.
Browser configurationOnly deliberately public values belong in VITE_ settings; no server credentials or evidence tokens.

Release checklist

  1. Identify exact parent/submodule/package revisions and intended deployment topology.
  2. Run builds and meaningful owning-service tests; resolve tracked release blockers and record exceptions explicitly.
  3. Rehearse additive migrations on representative restored fixtures; verify constraints and balance/row reconciliation.
  4. Back up data and immutable evidence; identify application rollback and data-forward-recovery boundaries.
  5. Apply migrations in the release step, not an untrusted preview build; deploy compatible services/consumers.
  6. Smoke-test authentication, tenant isolation, intake/review, financial states and provider failure handling in staging.
  7. Record release evidence and accountable approval; monitor jobs, reconciliation exceptions and external-provider outcomes.

Incident and recovery actions

SymptomInitial response
Job interrupted / provider timeoutInspect persisted job/execution/artifacts; do not blindly replay side effects. Current worker marks interrupted jobs failed for explicit review.
Email send outcome uncertainReconcile provider/SMTP evidence before retrying; successful request acceptance does not prove delivery.
Payment or funding outcome uncertainLook up the persisted operation and provider reference; reconcile before any retry that could create another obligation.
Stale quote/workbench/versionRefresh and review the exact active revision; preserve historical snapshots instead of overwriting.
Database restore / cross-service mismatchRestore evidence and version references, then reconcile parties/currencies/operations across services before financial writes resume.

Documentation maintenance checklist

  • Update the relevant child page and source references when a service contract, schema, calculation or workflow changes.
  • Distinguish local verification, staging evidence and production results with dates and exact scope.
  • Link new defects/gaps to the correct Jira epic; preserve evidence when closing them.
  • Review stale assumptions around authentication, pipeline automation and binding: older repository documents describe superseded behavior.
